# sego tool test corpus

The recorded stdout of the reference setools tools for the queries in
[`../tools.txt`](../tools.txt), one file per case (`<case>.txt`), used by
`tools_integration_test.go`.

The cases cover `seinfo`, `sediff`, `sedta`, `seinfoflow` and `sechecker` on
the policy fixtures in [`../policies`](../policies) (generated by
[`../gen.sh`](../gen.sh)) plus the fixtures from `policy/testdata`. The
`sechecker` configurations and the permission map live in
[`../checker`](../checker) and [`../perm_map`](../perm_map).

The goldens are recordings of a throw-away build of the in-tree setools 4.8
(the same build the `sesearch` corpus was recorded from). Regenerate them with

```
bash testdata/gen_tools_expected.sh           # record
bash testdata/gen_tools_expected.sh --check   # reproduce into a temp dir
```

The default oracle is `ORACLE_PYTHON` + `ORACLE_DIR` (a Python interpreter and
a tree containing the built `setools` package and the CLI scripts):

| variable       | default                                                    |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `ORACLE_PYTHON`| `/tmp/setools48/venv312/bin/python`                        |
| `ORACLE_DIR`   | `/tmp/setools48`                                           |
| `SETOOLS_ENV`  | `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<libselinux>/src:<libsepol>/src`          |

Outputs that setools renders in Python `set` or hash table order (the modified
rule permission lists, modified extended permission rule order, MLS alias
order) are not reproducible; the corpus avoids those cases, and where they can
still appear the verbose `sechecker` timestamps are stripped. See the
"Divergences from setools" section of the top-level README.
